automated_attempt.result: exit 3, insufficient signal, no colors found
automated_attempt.reason: no dedicated marketing/docs site exists for this project (homepage field empty); the GitHub repo page itself is GitHub's own theme, not the project's, so the CSS/meta-theme-color heuristics found nothing to mine

manual_assisted_extraction.method: the project's own visible identity was pulled directly from its authored visual assets in the repo, per routine Step 6.3 (native-assisted): the logo lockup PNG (rendered by the author) and the demo.gif (the real TUI, screen-captured from the actual tool)

findings.logo_accent: #1fb6ff -- dominant saturated color in the official wordmark lockup (hue 200deg, sat 0.88, val 1.00), sampled by pixel-frequency analysis (Pillow) after excluding near-black/near-white pixels
findings.tui_canvas: #12161c -- most frequent pixel color across two sampled demo.gif frames (the real terminal background the tool renders on), near-black but not pure #000
findings.tui_secondary_accent: #00a6a4 -- the app's own 'live session' highlight/badge teal, fully saturated (hue 179deg), seen in the sessions[] active-row bar and the mcpsnoop corner label -- confirms the identity is a cool blue/teal family, not a one-off logo choice
findings.tui_foreground_note: the terminal's literal rendered foreground text sampled at ~#c7c6c6-#d8d7d8 (luma ~190-210), which is a typical dim default terminal gray -- too dim to clear the dark-canvas ink floor (>=230 luma), so ink was NOT copied verbatim; a near-white cool-toned ink was assembled instead, consistent with the same hue family (see token_provenance)
findings.excluded: a warm rust/orange (~#4f2b26, hue 7-10deg) also appears in the demo frames but belongs to the Claude Code app icon shown incidentally in the demo, not to mcpsnoop's own identity -- excluded from the palette

verdict: native-assisted -- brand_slug: mcpsnoop-native-assisted. The accent (#1fb6ff) and canvas (#12161c) are both drawn directly from the author's own rendered assets (the logo and the live TUI), judged coherent against the visible identity of the tool by eye before adopting.
